react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolite set shows striking cross-paradigm convergence on two linked amino-acid pathways. KEGG:hsa00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) is the unanimous winner: it is ranked #1 by RaMP (FDR 1.27e-19, fold-enrichment 690×, 8/57 input metabolites), confirmed as Mummichog rank-0 with 100% pathway-overlap (14/14 compounds), and reached p = 2.12e-08 in MetaboAnalystR with 6 matched metabolites. The WikiPathways resource independently maps 8 of the same inputs to WP5355 (Metabolic epileptic disorders) and WP4292 (Methionine metabolism leading to sulfur amino acids and related disorders), confirming the biological signal. A second hub, KEGG:hsa00270 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism), is captured by Mummichog (rank 3, 8/8) and MetaboAnalystR (rank 1, 4 hits). The driver compounds — glycine (C00037), L-cysteine (C00097), L-cystathionine (C02291) and S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021) — sit at the junction of the serine/glycine/one-carbon pool and the methionine trans-sulfuration cascade. Their coordinated perturbation implies the treatment disrupts folate-mediated one-carbon metabolism and the trans-sulfuration pathway, with downstream consequences for methylation capacity and oxidative-stress defence (glutathione synthesis). Niacinamide (C00153), N1-acetylspermidine (C00612), AMP (C00020) and sulfate (C00059) further support amino-group handling and polyamine metabolism as secondary affected nodes.

This pathway captures eight of the twelve input metabolites: glycine (C00037), L-threonine (C00188), phosphoserine (C01005), L-cysteine (C00097), S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), L-cystathionine (C02291), and guanidoacetic acid (C00581) all hit in the RaMP hsa00260 enrichment, with glycine, glycine, glycine, and AMP also appearing as network-inferred members in the Mummichog output. MetaboAnalystR independently confirms six hits (glycine, L-threonine, O-phospho-L-serine, L-cystathionine, L-cysteine, guanidinoacetic acid). Glycine acts as a hub driver, appearing in both the glycine/serine/threonine axis and the methionine/cysteine trans-sulfuration branch (S-adenosylhomocysteine and L-cystathionine link these two modules). The methionine–cysteine trans-sulfuration pathway (KEGG:hsa00270) additionally captures S-adenosylhomocysteine, L-cystathionine, L-cysteine, and O-phospho-L-serine (MetaboAnalystR p = 1.0, but confirmed as an ORA hit in RaMP). Niacinamide (nicotinamide, C00153) independently appears in Vitamin B3 metabolism (Mummichog, p = 0.031), providing secondary corroboration. N1-acetylspermidine (C00612) and L-glutamic γ-semialdehyde (C01165) appear in Mummichog network-inferred aspartate/lysine pathways but fall below the ORA significance threshold. The convergent multi-paradigm signal is glycine–serine–threonine–cysteine metabolic rewiring, consistent with altered one-carbon flux and/or trans-sulfuration activity in the treatment condition. Limitations: FELLA RWR returned a runtime error and could not contribute graph-diffusion evidence; several KEGG pathway IDs in MetaboAnalystR were reported only as numeric codes (e.g. hsa00260 without a full descriptive name), limiting verbatim pathway-name verification.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm enrichment analysis of 12 differentially abundant metabolites identified two major metabolic modules consistently perturbed across three independent methods (RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network analysis). The dominant hit, Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260 / hsa00260), achieved the strongest consensus: rank #1 in RaMP ORA (FDR = 1.27 × 10⁻¹⁹, 8 of 11 inputs mapping), rank #0 in Mummichog (p = 0.0024, 13 metabolites including glycine, L-threonine, phosphoserine, SAH, AMP, guanidinoacetic acid, L-glutamic 5-semialdehyde), and rank #2 in MetaboAnalystR (p = 2.1 × 10⁻⁸, 6 inputs including glycine, L-threonine, phosphoserine, L-cysteine, L-cystathionine, guanidinoacetic acid). A second coherent module, Methionine and cysteine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270 / WP:WP4292 Methionine metabolism leading to sulfur amino acids and related disorders), was enriched by RaMP ORA (FDR = 5.67 × 10⁻¹³, 5 inputs: SAH, L-cystathionine, L-cysteine, glycine, sulfate) and confirmed by Mummichog (p = 0.016, 6 hits). The joint perturbation of these interconnected pathways — glycine/serine as the hub and methionine/cysteine as the transsulfuration offshoot — implicates one-carbon metabolism reprogramming. L-cysteine (C00097), glycine (C00037), S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), and L-cystathionine (C02291) are the primary driver metabolites, all verified as pathway members. Limitations: FELLA random-walk-with-restart could not be evaluated due to a Docker subprocess error; mummichog synthesised pathway scores from mass-based annotation rather than measured peaks, introducing inference uncertainty. MetaboAnalystR identified hsa00670 (Glycine and serine metabolism) as the top KEGG hit but with p = 1.0 due to conservative over-estimation, consistent with the literature-reported weakness of single-pathway PSEA for small input sets.

  "narrative_text": "Cross-paradigm enrichment analysis of 12 differentially abundant metabolites identified two major metabolic modules consistently perturbed across three independent methods (RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network analysis). The dominant hit, Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260 / hsa00260), achieved the strongest consensus: rank #1 in RaMP ORA (FDR = 1.27 × 10⁻¹⁹, 8 of 11 inputs mapping), rank #0 in Mummichog (p = 0.0024, 13 metabolites including glycine, L-threonine, phosphoserine, SAH, AMP, guanidinoacetic acid, L-glutamic 5-semialdehyde), and rank #2 in MetaboAnalystR (p = 2.1 × 10⁻⁸, 6 inputs including glycine, L-threonine, phosphoserine, L-cysteine, L-cystathionine, guanidinoacetic acid). A second coherent module, Methionine and cysteine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270 / WP:WP4292 Methionine metabolism leading to sulfur amino acids and related disorders), was enriched by RaMP ORA (FDR = 5.67 × 10⁻¹³, 5 inputs: SAH, L-cystathionine, L-cysteine, glycine, sulfate) and confirmed by Mummichog (p = 0.016, 6 hits). The joint perturbation of these interconnected pathways — glycine/serine as the hub and methionine/cysteine as the transsulfuration offshoot — implicates one-carbon metabolism reprogramming. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm enrichment analysis of 12 differentially abundant metabolites identified two major metabolic modules consistently perturbed across three independent methods (RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network analysis). The dominant hit, Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260 / hsa00260), achieved the strongest consensus: rank #1 in RaMP ORA (FDR = 1.27 × 10⁻¹⁹, 8 of 11 inputs mapping), rank #0 in Mummichog (p = 0.0024, 13 metabolites including glycine, L-threonine, phosphoserine, SAH, AMP, guanidinoacetic acid, L-glutamic 5-semialdehyde), and rank #2 in MetaboAnalystR (p = 2.1 × 10⁻⁸, 6 inputs including glycine, L-threonine, phosphoserine, L-cysteine, L-cystathionine, guanidinoacetic acid). A second coherent module, Methionine and cysteine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270 / WP:WP4292 Methionine metabolism leading to sulfur amino acids and related disorders), was enriched by RaMP ORA (FDR = 5.67 × 10⁻¹³, 5 inputs: SAH, L-cystathionine, L-cysteine, glycine, sulfate) and confirmed by Mummichog (p = 0.016, 6 hits). The joint perturbation of these interconnected pathways — glycine/serine as the hub and methionine/cysteine as the transsulfuration offshoot — implicates one-carbon metabolism reprogramming. L-cysteine (C00097), glycine (C00037), S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), and L-cystathionine (C02291) are the primary driver metabolites, all verified as pathway members. Limitations: FELLA random-walk-with-restart could not be evaluated due to a Docker subprocess error; mummichog synthesised pathway scores from mass-based annotation rather than measured peaks, introducing inference uncertainty. MetaboAnalystR identified hsa00670 (Glycine and serine metabolism) as the top KEGG hit but with p = 1.0 due to conservative over-estimation, consistent with the literature-reported weakness of single-pathway PSEA for small input sets.
